section_path: 6.1 Long-term Impact on the Banking Industry

note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM F, team 1916375: a fuzzy-comprehensive evaluation of a proposed global digital currency
system - three return measures, two cost measures, an AHP weighting and a net-income criterion -
then country choices by size, a trilemma argument, and a dynamic model of the banking industry.
Twenty-three pages, fourteen of which carry art, twenty-two measured regions.

**All twenty-two are accounted**: 12 figure rows for 11 numbered figures (Figure 11 is a
two-panel composite and takes two rows), 4 grids (the three numbered tables plus the uncaptioned
notation roster on p6), and 6 refusals. The refusals are the summary sheet's blue banner on p2,
three nested detections around the framed prose callout that sits beside Figure 2 on p6, and two
blocks of body text the layout pass measured on p7 and p8.

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 1.2 "Restatement of the Problem" takes **Figure 1**, the roadmap mind map, at the top of p5,
  with nothing said about it.
- 2.1 "Assumptions" takes **Figure 2**, the game matrix, hung between the assumption it argues
  and the sentence that states its consequence.
- 2.2 "Terms, Definitions and Symbols" takes the **p6 notation roster** - uncaptioned, unnumbered,
  starting straight under the heading.
- 3.3.1 and 3.3.2 take **Figures 3 and 4**: one construction, printed twice, short run then long
  run, eight lines apart on p9.
- 3.4, 3.5 and 3.6 take **Tables 1, 2 and 3** - one grid per subsection, each opening its page.
- 4.1.1 and 4.1.2 take **Figures 6 and 7**: the large-country and small-country loanable-funds
  schematic, one question asked twice.
- 4.2 takes **Figure 5**, the trilemma triangle, immediately after the sentence that states its
  conclusion.
- 4.2.2 takes **Figures 8 and 9**: the floating-rate pair and the fixed-rate schematic, one page
  apart.
- 5.4 "Conclusion" takes **Figure 10**, the regulatory ring scheme.
- 6.1 takes **Figure 11**, the two-panel long-term banking impact.

The pattern is one exhibit per subsection, and the exhibit always lands *after* the paragraph
that has finished the argument and *before* the sentence that draws the conclusion from it. No
subsection carries two exhibits except where the pair is the point (3.3, 4.1).

## When it goes 3-D

**Never.** Twelve figure rows, zero perspective projection, zero surface, zero isometric
drawing, no colourbar anywhere. The paper's three variables - return, cost, weighting - are
handled by three separate two-variable schematics and three flat grids, never by a third axis.
The only depth cue in the whole file is the drop shadow under the pictogram cells of Figure 2,
which is decoration on a pasted image.

## What the figures do

| group | count | what it actually is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Figure 1 | 1 | radial mind map: a cloud, two stacks of ovals, five method boxes |
| Figure 2 | 1 | 2x2 payoff matrix, pasted pictograms, blue frame, drop shadow |
| Figures 3, 4 | 2 | money market: two solid curves, then the same pair doubled in dashed shift |
| Figures 6, 7 | 2 | loanable funds, two straight lines, the second carrying an NX brace |
| Figure 5 | 1 | trilemma triangle with two double-headed arrows |
| Figures 8, 9 | 2 | the same two-panel arrowed schematic drawn twice, floating then fixed |
| Figure 10 | 1 | ring-and-node scheme: an annulus, two green circulation arrows, a six-node web |
| Figure 11 | 1 (2 panels) | side-by-side banking simulations |
| Tables 1-3 | 3 | pasted colour-blocked grids |
| p6 roster | 1 | booktabs notation list, uncaptioned |

**Not one chart in the file has a numeric axis.** The six economics diagrams carry arrowed axes
with named levels only ('r_0' over 'r*', 'M_D', 'M*', 'M_S', 'r_1' over 'r_0'), and every curve
is labelled in place, so no figure in the paper needs a legend. There is no bar, no histogram, no
scatter, no box plot, no heatmap, no map and no time series anywhere: the family vocabulary of
this paper is exactly {mind map, payoff matrix, line schematic, triangular schematic}.

## Table shapes worth reusing

| table | shape | trick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p6 roster | 16x2, header 1 | navy header band, zebra body, one white divider, no side frames |
| Table 1 | 5x7, header 2 | two-tier header: a spanning factor band over a repeated 'Great(v1) Small(v2)' pair |
| Table 2 | 5x7, header 2 | Table 1's construction reused unchanged, one section and one subject later |
| Table 3 | 7x8, header 1 | pairwise matrix plus its weight column, printed 1s on the diagonal |

Three numbered grids, one construction: pasted colour-blocked images with a thin top rule, a
rule under the header, a thin bottom rule, vertical rules between every block, and **no
inter-row rules at all** - the blocks are held apart by fill colour instead. The caption always
prints above. Only the uncaptioned roster is a booktabs grid, and it is the only one with zebra
stripes.

## Caption template

**One dialect, no seam.** All fourteen captions are `Number: phrase`, colon attached, one space
after it, and every one of them is a noun phrase naming the quantity, never a sentence:

- `Figure 1: Overview of Our Work`
- `Figure 2: Game Theory analysis about the necessity of the Central Bank`
- `Figure 3:interest rate analysis in short term` (the file's one spacing fault)
- `Figure 5: Impossible Trinity Theory`
- `Table 2: the member ship of factors Cr1 , Cr2 , Cr3` (the file's one spelling fault)
- `Table 3: AHP Weight and Impact`

Captions print BELOW all eleven figures and ABOVE all three grids. No caption carries a unit, a
parameter value or a conclusion; the variable symbols in the caption are set in italic with
subscripts, which is why the text layer leaves spaces around them ('Rindividual , Rnation ,
Rglobal'). This is the opposite of #186, where the colon arrived mid-paper: here the single
dialect dates the whole document to one typesetting pass.

## Context connectives

- **Only one exhibit is ever named by number**: `in the figure 2` on p5, lower case, with no space
  before the next word's capital. Every other exhibit is found by position.
- The pointer, when there is one, is a colon-ended deictic clause: `Next is the single factor
  coefficient matrix.` (Table 1), `Through easy analysis, we could empower these indicators as
  follows:` (Table 2), `We use the AHP method, then get the weight of R1, R2 , R3 , a1 , a2 , a3
  to NI as follow:` (Table 3), `They can be displayed as follow:` (Figure 6).
- **Twice the pointer refers to an equation, not to the figure beside it**: 'They can be
  displayed as follow:' introduces equation (32) and the schematic follows it, and 'as follow:'
  before Table 3 points at the AHP method two paragraphs up.
- Five exhibits get no pointer at all - Figures 1, 5, 7, 10 and Table 1's roster page - and three
  get no read-back: Table 3, Figure 5 and Figure 10 all end their subsection, so the next printed
  line is a heading.
- Figures 6 and 7 are introduced by two sentences that differ by one word ('In large countries,
  the interest rates are determined internally' / 'In small countries, ...'), which is how the
  paper signals that the second drawing is the first one re-parameterised.

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **The pasted tables do not exist in the text layer.** Tables 1, 2 and 3 are embedded images, so
  their own words ('Factors', 'Membership', 'Great(v1)', 'Small(v2)', 'Impact') appear on no page
  of the text layer while their captions do. Tables 1 and 2 additionally re-print the same nine
  numbers below as three typeset matrices numbered (17), and it is those matrices - not the
  tables - that the text layer holds.
- **The printed footer is offset by one**: PDF page 4 prints `Page 3 of 22`.
- **The table of contents parses as headings**: p3 carries '3.1.1 Model of Currency Value………6'
  and '6.3 Long-term Impact on International Relationship………20' as numbered section entries, so
  the heading index lists sections on the page they are listed on, not the page they start.
- **The caption detector misses a colon with no space**: `Figure 3:interest rate analysis in short
  term`. A caption regex demanding ': ' reads p9 as carrying an uncaptioned figure.
- **Sentences run together without a space** at several figure boundaries: `figure 2This trust
  mechanism`, `will rise Fixed Exchange Rate`, `Cr1 , Cr2 and Cr3 .Through easy analysis`. The
  paragraph break disappears while the period survives, so a sentence splitter that keeps
  sentence case will see one 60-word sentence where the page printed two.
- **The p6 roster's columns drift in the text layer**: `S(w,σ ) w` and `RT Ri labor input` are
  two rows whose meaning column has run into the next row's symbol, so the roster reads as 17
  rows in text against 15 printed.

## Declared deficits

**None.** Every measured region on the fourteen exhibit-bearing pages is either an exhibit row or
a documented refusal, the p6 roster is claimed as an uncaptioned grid rather than dropped, and
every caption the detector carries is quoted verbatim.
rules: Caption punctuation is a document-wide property here, not a running state: all fourteen captions are 'Number: phrase' with the colon attached, from p5 to p20, and there is no seam anywhere. 218 of the lane's 252 papers keep one dialect for the whole file; a clean single switch happens in only ten, which is what #186 did and this one does not. [caption.numbering]

The single caption spacing fault is per-paragraph, not per-paper: 'Figure 3:interest rate analysis in short term' loses the post-colon space while 'Figure 4: interest rate analysis in long term' on the same page keeps it. [caption.numbering]
Captions sit BELOW every figure and ABOVE every grid, including the pasted ones, and the rule never varies inside a class. [caption.position]

No caption carries a unit, a number, a parameter value or a conclusion; each is a noun phrase naming the quantity the object shows, and the only typographic oddity is that variable symbols are set in italic with subscripts, which is why the text layer pads them with spaces. [caption.variables]

Caption and grid numbering follows the argument, not the press: Figure 5 prints on p15, after Figures 6 and 7 on p14, because the trilemma belongs to section 4.2 and the loanable-funds pair to 4.1. [place.section_path]

Exactly one exhibit in the file is named by number in prose ('in the figure 2', lower case, glued to the next word's capital). Every other exhibit is located by the paragraph that hangs it and by its own caption. [mention.count]

The pointer of choice is a colon-ended deictic clause built on 'as follow(s)', and it points at the nearest typeset object, which is sometimes an equation two lines above the figure rather than the figure itself. [mention.lead_pattern]

Five exhibits get no pointer and three get no read-back; the read-back sentences, when they exist, explain the slope or the level of the drawn curves and never refer to the object by name. [mention.lead_sentence]

A pair of drawings is introduced by a pair of sentences that differ by one word ('In large countries ...' / 'In small countries ...'), which is the file's way of saying the second object is the first one re-parameterised - the same construction as the figures themselves. [mention.lead_sentence]

3-D is never a solution here: three variables become three separate two-variable schematics and three flat grids. The only depth cue in the file is a drop shadow on a pasted pictogram. [geometry.three_d]

Diagrams carry the model, and no chart in the file carries a numeric axis: the six economics schematics label arrowed axes with named levels only, so there is no per-axis scale anywhere and no numeric tick in twelve rows. [geometry.family]

No figure needs a legend because every series is labelled in place on its own curve ('r(M_supply)', 'CF(r)', 'NX(e)', 'r'(M_demand)'); where a line style carries the meaning (solid = original, dashed = shift) the decoded labels sit on the curves, not in a key. [geometry.legend]

A composite is used only when two markets must be read against one another: Figure 8 stacks two panels and draws red dotted verticals from the upper panel's x-levels down through the lower one, and Figure 11 puts two simulations side by side. Everything else is one object per number. [geometry.panel_count]

Shared axes are shared by registration, not by a shared title: Figure 8's two panels print different axis titles ('CF' above, 'NX' below) and are tied only by drawn guide lines. [geometry.shared_axes]

The three numbered grids are one construction repeated: pasted colour-blocked images with a thin top rule, a rule under the header, a thin bottom rule, vertical rules between the column blocks, and no inter-row rule at all - the blocks are separated by fill, not by lines. [table.rule_style]

A merged header cell is used to express a repeated measure, not to group a long label: the upper tier spans a pair of columns per factor ('R_individual', 'R_nation', 'R_global') and the lower tier repeats 'Great(v1)' 'Small(v2)' under every pair. [table.merged_cells]

Two identical grids one section apart reuse the construction without a single tweak - same seven columns, same two-tier header, same fills, same rules - and only the row labels and numbers change. [table.rule_style]

Zebra belongs to the one grid that has no caption: the p6 notation roster alternates shading on every other data row, while the three numbered grids shade by column block and never alternate. [table.zebra]

Numeric columns are not decimal-aligned in the numbered grids: the AHP matrix prints slash fractions ('1/3', '1/4') beside four-decimal weights, so alignment is impossible by construction. [table.decimal_aligned]
No grid in the file carries a units row, a source line or a note: every note-like statement about a table is printed as running prose before or after it. [table.note_sentence]
